sources.entry: Lychee - Grid and album based photo-management-system. (Source Code) MIT PHP/Docker
Lychee | Beautiful photo management and sharing

summary.one_liner: Lychee is a free, open-source, self-hosted photo management and sharing system that runs on your own server or web space.
summary.what_it_does: Lychee is a grid- and album-based photo management tool meant to be run on your own server or web space. The README says you can upload, manage, and share photos through a browser interface that it describes as feeling like a native application. It is positioned as including the essential features needed to keep photos stored on your own infrastructure. A Supporter Edition (SE) is mentioned as offering additional functionality. The README points to external documentation for installation, configuration, and updates, and to a changelog and website for further details. Docker is the recommended deployment route, using a Lychee container with a MariaDB database.
use_cases: upload and organize personal photos on own server
replace cloud photo sharing with a self-hosted option
run a photo website from a web space
how_to_run: curl -O <minimal docker-compose template URL from README>
Or use the recommended docker-compose.yaml with image ghcr.io/lycheeorg/lychee:latest and a mariadb:11 database container
Generate APP_KEY with: echo "base64:$(openssl rand -base64 32)" and set it in the environment
From source: requires PHP 8.4+, Composer, and npm (see documentation)
notable: Grid and album based photo layout with upload, management and sharing
Official Docker image on GitHub Container Registry and Docker Hub, with latest and edge tags
Minimal docker-compose option that includes a separate worker container for background jobs
Optional Supporter Edition (SE) with extra features
Version 7.0 changes the Docker image; an upgrade guide is provided
caveats: Version 7.0 introduces significant changes to the Docker image, so upgrading requires following the Upgrade Guide
Advanced features are reserved for the paid Supporter Edition (SE)
Recommended setup requires a separate database container and a generated APP_KEY
